description: Extend existing dark mode implementation to store theme preference in User model for authenticated users and sync theme across devices. ThemeService is complete and functional (frontend/src/app/service/theme.service.ts) with localStorage persistence. Add backend storage and sync: add theme field to User model, create PUT /api/users/profile/theme endpoint, update ThemeService to sync with backend when user is authenticated.
steps: 1. Read existing ThemeService at frontend/src/app/service/theme.service.ts to understand current localStorage-based implementation
2. Add theme field to User model at frontend/server/models/User.js: theme: { type: String, enum: ['light', 'dark'], default: 'light' }
3. Create PUT /api/users/profile/theme endpoint in frontend/server/routes/users.js with body { userId, theme }. Controller validates theme enum ['light', 'dark'] and updates user.theme

4. Update ThemeService at frontend/src/app/service/theme.service.ts: inject HttpClient and AuthService. Modify setTheme(theme) to: (a) update localStorage (existing), (b) apply theme class to body (existing), (c) if AuthService.currentUser exists, call PUT /api/users/profile/theme with userId and theme

5. Update AuthService at frontend/src/app/service/auth.service.ts: in restoreSession() after loading user from sessionStorage, check if user.theme exists. If yes, call ThemeService.setTheme(user.theme) to apply user's saved theme
6. Update login flow: after successful Google Sign-In and user data is fetched from backend, apply user.theme if it exists. This ensures theme syncs on login across devices
7. Test theme persistence: Sign in on device A, change theme to dark, sign out. Sign in on device B (or clear localStorage and sign in again), verify dark theme is applied automatically
8. Ensure theme toggle in navbar at frontend/src/app/Component/navbar/navbar.component.html is already wired to ThemeService.toggle(). Verify it works correctly

9. Add CSS variables for theme colors if not already present in global styles. Verify --color-navbar-bg, --color-text, --color-background, --color-primary are defined for both .light-theme and .dark-theme classes
10. Apply theme variables across all components: Verify booking cards, forms, buttons, modals use CSS variables so they respond to theme changes. Update any hardcoded colors to use var(--color-*)
11. Update translation keys if needed: verify THEME.LIGHT and THEME.DARK keys exist in en.json, hi.json, mr.json for potential future use in theme selector UI
acceptance_criteria: User model has theme field with enum validation ['light', 'dark']
PUT /api/users/profile/theme endpoint exists and updates user.theme
Theme preference syncs to backend when authenticated user toggles theme
Theme preference loads from backend on login and applies automatically
Anonymous users: theme persists in localStorage only (existing behavior preserved)
Authenticated users: theme persists in both localStorage and user profile, syncs across devices
Theme toggle in navbar works for both authenticated and anonymous users
All components use CSS variables for colors and respond to theme changes
No hardcoded light-mode-only colors remain in component styles
verification: cd /Users/kedarpatil/Documents/kedar/tedbus_project/REDBUS-CLONE-MEAN-main-3/.worktrees/tedbus-complete-upgrade/frontend && npm run build -- produces no TypeScript errors
Start backend and frontend, toggle theme without signing in, verify dark mode applies and persists in localStorage on reload
Sign in with Google, toggle theme to dark, verify PUT /api/users/profile/theme is called (check network tab)
Sign out, clear localStorage, sign in again, verify dark theme is applied automatically from user profile
Navigate to all pages (home, search, booking, payment, profile, community, route-planner) in dark mode and verify all elements render correctly with appropriate dark colors
